text: Name a tokenization algorithm or tokenizer
note: Algorithms, libraries and named vocabularies that split input into tokens; classic NLP, tokenizer-free and image/audio tokenizers count too

answers.q: Randomly skip merges during training so the model sees many segmentations of every word. Dropout for tokenizers.
Unsupervised morphological segmentation via minimum description length, born in Helsinki for Finnish.
A second BPE stage that merges across spaces, minting 'superword' tokens.
Learns its own chunk boundaries end to end. Tokenization as a layer.
Round each latent dimension to a few levels. VQ without the codebook collapse.
The ~200k-token vocabulary introduced with GPT-4o. Kinder to non-English text.
GPT-2 and GPT-3's 50,257 tokens, the last being <|endoftext|>.
tokenizer.perl from the Moses MT toolkit. A Perl script that outlived its decade.
NLTK's unsupervised sentence splitter. It learns abbreviations so 'Dr.' doesn't end a sentence.
Greedy longest-match-first: WordPiece's inference and an old trick for Chinese segmentation.
Unknown characters break into UTF-8 byte tokens instead of <unk>. Llama's SentencePiece does it.
Chinese for 'stutter': the go-to Python library for Chinese word segmentation.
The classic Japanese morphological analyzer, named after its author's favorite food, mekabu.
'An Image is Worth 16x16 Words': ViT's tokenizer is a strided linear projection.
Meta's tokenizer-free model: start a new byte patch wherever next-byte entropy spikes.
Fixed-size byte patches, a global transformer over patches and a local one within them.
Mistral's tiktoken-based tokenizer since NeMo, ~30% more efficient on code and many languages.
OpenAI's fast BPE library: cl100k_base, o200k_base and friends.
The ~100k-token vocabulary behind GPT-3.5-turbo and GPT-4.
Start huge and prune: keep the vocab that maximizes a unigram LM's likelihood. Kudo, 2018.
GPT-2's trick: run BPE over raw bytes, so no input is ever <unk>.
Philip Gage's 1994 compression algorithm, repurposed for NMT by Sennrich et al. in 2016.
Schuster & Nakajima 2012, for Japanese and Korean voice search. Later BERT's ##pieces.
Treats text as a raw stream, spaces included (▁). No pre-tokenization, any language.
